questions.q: Which earlier chapter's catalog-info.yaml and template.yaml concepts did Lesson 29's golden-path template directly extend?
options: Chapter 7, Platform Observability and Developer Experience
Chapter 2, Building a Developer Self-Service Portal
Chapter 5, Advanced CI/CD Pipeline Design
Chapter 3, GitOps Principles
questions.explain: Chapter 2 introduced the software catalog and the scaffolder template; Lesson 29 turned those exact concepts into a real, runnable golden path.

questions.q: Why did Lesson 30's canary rollout count as 'still GitOps, start to finish,' according to this review?
options: Because Argo Rollouts replaces ArgoCD entirely during a canary
Because canary rollouts never actually touch the GitOps repo
Because Prometheus queries are considered part of Git by definition
Because the Rollout and AnalysisTemplate were just more YAML in the same overlay reconciled by the Application model from Chapter 4
questions.explain: Chapter 4's Application reconciliation model is exactly what let traffic shift and roll back automatically while the whole process stayed visible in Git and ArgoCD.

questions.q: According to this review, which chapter is Lesson 31's case study built directly on?
options: Chapter 7, Platform Observability and Developer Experience
Chapter 6, Pipeline-as-Code at Scale
Chapter 1, Platform Engineering Fundamentals, exclusively
Chapter 4, GitOps in Practice
questions.explain: Northfield's first failure was never instrumenting the platform or its users' experience -- precisely what Chapter 7 teaches a platform team to do from day one.

questions.q: Why does this course close without naming a single 'next course,' unlike most courses in this path?
options: Because it is the final course in the entire Cloud Engineer to Cloud Architect path
Because the path has not yet defined what comes after Expert Specialization
Because it is the first of four Expert Specialization courses that build on Advanced Specialization but not on each other, so they can be taken in any order
Because the platform built in this capstone was never actually adopted
questions.explain: This course is one of four Expert Specialization courses -- alongside Hybrid & Multi-Cloud Enterprise Architecture, AI Cloud Infrastructure/GPU Computing/MLOps, and Advanced SRE/Disaster Recovery/Resilience -- that don't depend on each other.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the real job of platform engineering that this capstone proved, beyond building a technically correct platform?
options: Choosing ArgoCD over Flux for every future project
Building a platform that also earns the adoption it needs to actually matter
Avoiding canary rollouts in favor of all-at-once deploys
Memorizing every Backstage entity kind that exists
questions.explain: The capstone's real lesson, reinforced by Lesson 31's case study, is that a platform also has to earn adoption -- technical correctness alone isn't the whole job.
